summary: The main article describes a cooperative photoredox and N-heterocyclic carbene-catalyzed acylation of aryl cyclopropanes. It includes 2 tables for optimization and substrate scope, and 6 schemes detailing the reaction strategy, applications, and mechanism.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Selected application examples of bioactive cyclopropane.
items.description: Illustrates various pharmaceutical molecules containing cyclopropane rings, such as Cabozantinib and Lemborexant.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Functionalization of strained cyclopropanes.
items.description: Compares traditional directed C-H functionalization and [3+n] annulation with the proposed deconstruction-reconstruction strategy.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Reaction optimization a
items.description: Lists the screening of NHC catalysts, photocatalysts, bases, and solvents to optimize the yield of product 3aa.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Scope of substrates acyl imidazoles and aryl cyclopropanes a
items.description: Displays the chemical structures and yields for various acylated cyclopropane products synthesized using the optimized conditions.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: ' One-pot, two-step ' acylation reaction from carboxylic acid.
items.description: Demonstrates a practical one-pot procedure starting from carboxylic acids to form acylated cyclopropanes.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Esteri fi cation of cyclopropane 1a and further transformation.
items.description: Shows the extension of the method to esterification and the synthesis of a Lumacaftor skeleton derivative.

items.heading: Scheme 5
items.caption: Control experiments and linear relationship between I 0/ I and the concentration of 1a and 9 .
items.description: Presents radical trapping experiments and Stern-Volmer quenching studies to support the proposed mechanism.

items.heading: Scheme 6
items.caption: Plausible reaction mechanism.
items.description: Proposes a catalytic cycle involving photoredox oxidation of cyclopropane and NHC-mediated ketyl radical formation.
